(a) In General.—Section 303(g)(2)(B) of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 823(g)(2)(B)) is amended by striking clause (iv). 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 303(g)(2)(B) of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 823(g)(2)(B)) is amended in clause (iii) by striking “In any case” and all that follows through “the total” and inserting “The total”. 
    (c) Effective Date.—This section shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to the Controlled Substances Act, striking a clause, conforming the text, and setting an effective date. No tempting reading exists: it involves no consultation, comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section contains only technical amendments to existing statutory text and an effective date. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, public comment, or participation by non-federal entities in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Section 303(g)(2)(B) of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 823(g)(2)(B)) is amended by striking clause (iv).
qwen_block.b:
1.  **Think briefly**: The section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Controlled Substances Act (striking specific clauses and inserting text) and an effective date provision. It does not create any new process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It is purely legislative drafting language modifying existing statutory text. There is no interaction with non-federal parties described here.

opus.w: The section only amends statutory text by striking a clause and rewording another, and sets an effective date. Nothing in it involves consulting outside parties, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, or a right to sue. The tempting reading is that the struck clause concerned rulemaking, but removing a rulemaking power does not require or invite any outside participation.
opus.s: Section 303(g)(2)(B) of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 823(g)(2)(B)) is amended by striking clause (iv).
opus.b:
I've labelled this section **No**.

1. **The tempting reading:** Section 303(g)(2)(B) of the Controlled Substances Act covers patient limits for practitioners who prescribe certain addiction-treatment drugs. If I recall it correctly, the struck clause (iv) let the Secretary change those limits by regulation, and rulemaking counts as participation. But that clause isn't quoted here. Even if my memory is right, this section removes that rulemaking power rather than creating it.
2. **Against the definition:** The section only strikes and rewords text and sets an effective date. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutory text (striking clauses and inserting words) and sets an effective date. It does not establish any new advisory bodies, comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with outside parties. The text describes legislative changes to the law itself, not a participatory process for decision-making.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the Controlled Substances Act could implicitly affect public participation rights (e.g., in scheduling drugs), but the text itself only describes technical amendments to statutory clauses and an effective date. It does not explicitly create, require, or describe any process for outside parties to participate in a decision.
